newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices gain ahead of cooler temps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices gain ahead of cooler temps.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices for April climbed Monday by almost 10 cents, helped by forecasts for cooler Midwest and eastern weather later this week and prospects for some injection demand, sources said.
Traders said favorable spreads should stir some early injection buying and help support physical prices near-term.
"Storage buying and weather are moving things up," said one Texas-based trader, noting the 40-cent May-Dec spread.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, swing prices at Henry Hub firmed almost 10 cents to near the $2 per mmBtu mark, more than 15 cents over the April index.
In south Texas, prices were up more than a nickel to the mid-to-high $1.80s, also more than 15 cents over April 1 levels.
In the Appalachian region, Columbia gained more than five cents to the low-teens.
Gas at the New York city gate was talked about 15 cents higher in the mid-$2.20s, about seven cents above index.
Midcontinent prices, helped by cooler weather there, climbed Monday by more than 10 cents to the mid-to-high $1.80s, also 15 cents above monthly indices.
West Texas gas in the Permian basin firmed more than five cents to $1.75-1.80. At the southern California border, spot prices were seven cents higher in the mid-to-high $1.80s.
